app: LinkedIn (Community Management API for Company Page posting)
summary: Sign In with LinkedIn (OpenID Connect) and Share on LinkedIn (w_member_social, posting as a person) are self-serve and work within minutes. Posting as a Company Page needs w_organization_social, and that only comes with the vetted Community Management API. Access is limited to registered legal organizations with a business email, and the app must be verified by the super admin of your LinkedIn Page. You get a rate-limited Development tier first, then apply for Standard tier with a screencast. LinkedIn publishes no review time; plan on weeks, and a rejection means starting over with a new app.

verdict.launchNote: First token: 15 min for openid/profile/email + w_member_social (personal posts); Company Page posting has no first token until Development tier is approved. 4-10 weeks (Development tier vetting reported at 1-3+ weeks, then build, then Standard tier review with screencast); no official SLA.
verdict.reviewRequired: Community Management API Development tier access form (legal org, business email, Page-verified app, approved use case), then Standard tier access form with screencast, test credentials and privacy policy review

evidence.note: The time range is anecdotal: LinkedIn documents no review time; a 2026 Q&A post cites a '10-14 business days' portal message for Development tier.

testMode.limits: Before approval only the open permissions work (openid, profile, email, w_member_social: posting as yourself, not as a Page). Development tier: 500 calls per app and 100 per member per 24 h, no BATCH_GET, social-action webhooks disabled. Integration must be finished within 12 months. Access tokens last 60 days; programmatic refresh tokens (365 days) come only with approved Marketing API (MDP) access such as Community Management, not with the self-serve products.

prerequisites.item: A LinkedIn Company Page for the developer's organization, with a super admin who approves the app association (30-day window; the association is permanent)
Registered legal organization: legal name, registered address, website

evidence.note: Comes from the profile's legalEntity; the legal name and address must match your registration documents.

prerequisites.item: Verified business email (personal addresses fail vetting)

evidence.note: An address on the company's own domain should pass.

prerequisites.item: Website and domain that match the organization
App logo and name without any part of the LinkedIn/Microsoft names or logos
Screencast (high-resolution, downloadable, narration recommended) and test credentials, for Standard tier

evidence.note: Use your HTTPS production callback. Docs say to add redirect URLs via HTTPS; an http://localhost entry may not be accepted.

steps.title: Create or confirm your LinkedIn Company Page
steps.detail: Create the Page under a real member account (no fake/headless profiles) and set its website to your company domain. Business verification on LinkedIn's side is checked against this Page and domain.

steps.title: Create a NEW developer app just for Community Management
steps.detail: linkedin.com/developers/apps/new: name, your Company Page, privacy policy URL, logo. Don't add Sign In with LinkedIn or other products to this app first. LinkedIn only lets you request Community Management on new apps that have no other API products. Use a separate app for login if you need one.

steps.title: Have the Page super admin verify the app
steps.detail: Settings tab > Verify. Send the verification request to a super admin of your Company Page, who has 30 days to approve. Unverified apps fail Development tier vetting.

steps.title: Add redirect URL and generate a test token
steps.detail: Auth tab: add the absolute HTTPS callback (no #, query ignored). Use the Token Generator or the 3-legged flow. Before approval only open scopes are listed.

fields.label: Authorized redirect URLs for your app

steps.title: Apply for Community Management API Development tier
steps.detail: Products tab > Community Management API > access form. Give the legal name, registered address, website, privacy policy and business email (then verify the email), and describe the use case: your app posts to each customer's own Page on their behalf. Read the restricted use cases first. An agent can draft the use-case text; a human submits.

steps.title: Build the Page-posting flow within Development tier limits
steps.detail: Implement OAuth with w_organization_social + r_organization_social (+ rw_organization_admin to list Pages via /organizationAcls). Post with the Posts API using the organization URN as author. Stay under 500 calls/app/day, and finish within 12 months.

steps.title: Record the Standard tier screencast
steps.detail: Page Management use case: show the full OAuth approval, a post going to the LinkedIn Page from the app, how a member's comment on it appears in the app, and which commenter profile fields are shown. Use high resolution and a downloadable file, show only your app's screens, and narrate.

steps.title: Apply for Standard tier
steps.detail: My Apps > Products > Standard tier access form: company and product overview, use case, test credentials, screencast. LinkedIn reviews against privacy policy, terms, security and data-storage rules, and may decline at its discretion. A rejection means a new app and a new Development tier application.
steps.estimate: 1 h hands-on; weeks of waiting (no published SLA)

steps.title: Handle 60-day token expiry
steps.detail: Access tokens last 60 days, and programmatic refresh tokens (valid 365 days) are issued only to apps approved for the Marketing Developer Platform, which Community Management access is part of; self-serve apps (Sign In, Share on LinkedIn) get none. Without refresh tokens, re-run the authorization flow (silent if the member is still logged in) before expiry. If you change scopes, users must re-consent, and earlier tokens are invalidated.

scopes.name: w_organization_social
scopes.purpose: Create posts, comments and reactions as a Company Page the user administers
scopes.note: Only via the Community Management (or Advertising) API. The member must be an admin of that Page.

scopes.name: r_organization_social
scopes.purpose: Read the Page's own posts and engagement to confirm publication and report results

scopes.name: rw_organization_admin
scopes.purpose: List the Pages the member administers and read Page analytics
scopes.note: Restricted to organizations where the member has the ADMINISTRATOR role.

scopes.name: w_member_social
scopes.purpose: Post as the authenticated person (e.g. a team member's own profile), not as the Page
scopes.note: Open via the self-serve Share on LinkedIn product. Using it with an organization author returns HTTP 400 'Organization permissions must be used when using organization as author'.

scopes.name: openid profile email
scopes.purpose: Identify the staff member who connects LinkedIn
scopes.note: Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect, self-serve. Put it on a separate app from Community Management.

blockers.title: No registered legal entity on file
blockers.detail: Community Management is only for registered legal organizations with commercial use cases. LinkedIn checks the organization, website/domain and business email.
blockers.workaround: Fill legalEntity in the profile, make the Page website your company domain, and use an email on that domain.

blockers.title: Rejection burns the app
blockers.detail: A rejected Development or Standard tier request can't be re-applied for on the same app. You must create a new app and start again with Development tier.
blockers.workaround: Prepare every field and the screencast before submitting.

blockers.title: Community Management must be alone on a new app
blockers.detail: The access request is greyed out on apps that already have other API products (e.g. Sign In with LinkedIn), so login and Page posting end up as two apps.

blockers.title: Data rules conflict with lead tracking
blockers.detail: Member data (commenters, reactors) may not be used to create leads or enrich a CRM, may not be combined with other data, may only be displayed in the app, and social activity data may be stored for 48 hours at most. An assistant that turns LinkedIn commenters into leads would be a restricted use case.
blockers.workaround: Keep the LinkedIn use case to publishing and Page analytics. Don't feed member data into lead tracking.

blockers.title: Standard tier is discretionary
blockers.detail: LinkedIn may decline to upgrade even when the minimum requirements are met, and Development tier access lapses if the integration isn't completed within 12 months.

blockers.title: No review SLA, weak support routing
blockers.detail: LinkedIn publishes no turnaround. A 2026 report describes 14+ business days at 'Access Form Review' with support cases routed to the wrong teams.

agentCan: Draft the Development and Standard tier use-case text from the profile
Check the request against LinkedIn's restricted-use-cases list before submission
Implement the 3-legged OAuth flow, Posts API with organization author, and /organizationAcls Page listing
Write the screencast script for the Page Management test cases
Track 60-day token expiry and prompt re-consent; respect Development tier rate limits
youMust: Create the Company Page and developer app with a real LinkedIn account
Get a Page super admin to verify the app
Supply the legal entity details and verify the business email
Submit both access forms, record the screencast, provide reviewer test credentials

uncertainties: Review times are undocumented. The '10-14 business days' figure is one developer's transcription of the portal dialog (Aug 2026); a GitHub issue guessed '1-5 business days'.
Whether Sign In with LinkedIn can be added to the Community Management app after approval (the FAQ covers only the request time); we assume separate apps.
Whether LinkedIn accepts http://localhost redirect URLs; docs only say to add them via HTTPS.

Whether a multi-tenant tool (one app posting for several customers' Pages) needs anything beyond the standard Page Management use case. Not tested yet; the only first-hand observation is that Community Management needs an approved developer app.
Marketing version 202511 sunsets 2026-11-16; check the current API version header (li-lms-2026-10 is current).

verification.claim: OAuth endpoint behaviour (discovery metadata, PKCE, dynamic registration, unknown-client handling)
verification.note: LinkedIn's OIDC discovery lives under /oauth (root .well-known paths 404) and lists only openid/profile/email; it advertises no PKCE methods and no dynamic registration. Unknown client_id on /oauth/v2/authorization returns HTTP 200 with an HTML page.
